unit.title: Concessive Clauses
unit.subtitle: aunque, por más que and conceding what you don't know

grammar.title: ‘Even though’ vs ‘even if’ — the mood decides
grammar.intro: Concessive clauses set up an obstacle that fails to stop the main action. With aunque, the mood is the whole message: Aunque llueve, salgo concedes a real, known fact (it IS raining), while Aunque llueva, saldré concedes a hypothetical or immaterial one (rain or not, I'm going). Choosing indicative or subjunctive is a genuinely C1 skill — it lets you signal exactly how committed you are to the fact.

sections.heading: aunque: fact (indicative) vs concession (subjunctive)
sections.body: Use the indicative when you present the obstacle as a real, verified fact (‘even though’). Use the subjunctive when it's hypothetical, unknown, or you dismiss it as irrelevant (‘even if’ / ‘regardless of whether’). The present subjunctive also downgrades a known fact to ‘granted, but it doesn't matter’.

ex.es: Aunque está lloviendo, voy a salir a correr.
ex.en: Even though it's raining, I'm going out for a run.
Even if it rains tomorrow, I'll go out for a run.

sections.heading: Other concessive connectors
sections.body: A pesar de que works like aunque (indicative for fact, subjunctive for hypothesis). Por más/mucho que normally takes the subjunctive when conceding an unknown intensity. Aun cuando is an emphatic ‘even if/though’. Don't confuse aun (even) with aún (still/yet).
conj: in spite of the fact that
however much / no matter how much

ex.es: Por más que lo intentes, no vas a convencerlo.
ex.en: However hard you try, you won't convince him.

ex.es: A pesar de que ganaba bien, lo dejó todo.
ex.en: Despite the fact that he earned well, he gave it all up.

sections.heading: ‘si bien’ and ‘y eso que’: always indicative
sections.body: Two connectors resist the subjunctive entirely. Si bien (‘although’, formal/written) introduces a conceded real fact and takes the indicative. Y eso que (‘and that's even though’, colloquial and often tacked on afterward) is also always indicative. Both concede something you fully accept as true.

ex.es: Si bien reconozco el error, no me arrepiento.
ex.en: While I acknowledge the mistake, I don't regret it.

ex.es: Aprobó el examen, y eso que apenas estudió.
ex.en: He passed the exam — and that's despite hardly studying.

takeaways: aunque + indicative = conceded real fact (‘even though’); + subjunctive = hypothetical or dismissed (‘even if’).
a pesar de que mirrors aunque; por más/mucho que usually takes the subjunctive.
si bien and y eso que are always indicative — they concede accepted facts.

mistakes.w: Aunque tenga mucho dinero, ahora mismo no puedo pagarte.
mistakes.r: Aunque tengo mucho dinero, ahora mismo no puedo pagarte.
mistakes.why: You're conceding a real, current fact (you do have money), so use the indicative tengo, not the hypothetical tenga.

mistakes.w: Por más que lo intentas, no lo conseguirás.
mistakes.r: Por más que lo intentes, no lo conseguirás.
mistakes.why: por más que concedes an unknown future effort here, so it takes the subjunctive intentes.

mistakes.w: Si bien sea caro, merece la pena.
mistakes.r: Si bien es caro, merece la pena.
mistakes.why: si bien concedes an accepted fact and always takes the indicative: es, not sea.

exercises.prompt: Aunque no lo ___ ahora, algún día me lo agradecerás. (entender, tú)
exercises.prompt_en: Even though you may not understand it now, someday you'll thank me.
exercises.no: Here you concede it without asserting it as a plain fact, so the subjunctive fits: “entiendas”.

exercises.prompt: Aunque ___ carísimo, al final me compré el coche.
exercises.prompt_en: Even though it was really expensive, I ended up buying the car.
exercises.no: It's a real, verified past fact, so use the indicative: “era”.

exercises.prompt: Build: “However much you insist, I won't change my mind.”
exercises.no: “Por más que insistas, no cambiaré de idea” — por más que takes the subjunctive insistas.

exercises.prompt: Si bien la novela ___ larga, se lee en dos días. (ser)
exercises.prompt_en: Although the novel is long, you can read it in two days.
exercises.hint: si bien concedes an accepted fact → indicative of ser.
exercises.no: si bien always takes the indicative, so it's “es”.

exercises.prompt: Match each connector to its behaviour.
exercises.ok: ¡Excelente! Ya distingues concesión real de hipotética.

exercises.tts: Aunque me lo pidas de rodillas, no pienso ceder.
accepted: aunque me lo pidas de rodillas no pienso ceder
exercises.translation: Even if you beg me on your knees, I won't give in.
exercises.ok: ¡Correcto! “Aunque me lo pidas de rodillas, no pienso ceder.”
exercises.no: It was: “Aunque me lo pidas de rodillas, no pienso ceder.” (Even if you beg me on your knees, I won't give in.)

lines.speaker: Marcos
lines.es: El mercado está fatal. Quizá deberíamos posponer el lanzamiento.
lines.en: The market is terrible. Maybe we should postpone the launch.

options.text: Aunque el mercado esté mal, seguiremos adelante con el plan.
Aunque el mercado estará mal, seguiremos adelante con el plan.
Aunque el mercado sea mal, seguiremos adelante con el plan.

exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! Concesión que restas importancia → subjuntivo estar.
exercises.no: You're conceding it while dismissing its weight, and estar (not ser) describes a state: “Aunque el mercado esté mal”.

exercises.say: Aunque cueste, lo terminaremos a tiempo.
exercises.en: Even if it's hard, we'll finish it on time.
exercises.no: Almost — tap “Hear it”, then match the sound of “Aunque cueste, lo terminaremos a tiempo.”
